mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille from the designated Competent Authority; where the origin state is not an Apostille Party, consular legalization via the Canadian consular post

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-jurisdiction company registry (e.g., equivalent of Companies Registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Registry-issued certificate bearing an apostille, or consular legalization if Apostille Convention does not apply to the issuing state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and Hague Apostille (or consular legalization in non-Hague states)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, controllers, UBOs and authorized signatories against: (i) FINTRAC politically exposed persons ('PEP') categories and enhanced due-diligence rules; (ii) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List applicable to USD wire rails; (iii) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (iv) Global Affairs Canada sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act; (v) Criminal Code terrorism entity listings; and (vi) Interpol red notices and adverse-media sources. An enhanced screening file is required for non-Canadian resident UBOs and for counterparties in aviation spares trading because of controlled-goods and dual-use exposure.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta / Alberta Registries) - Corporate Name Search and Reservation portal, accessible directly or through registered agents
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Alberta corporate names must be expressed in the Latin alphabet, using English or French words, numerals, and prescribed punctuation. A non-Roman script name cannot be registered as the official corporate name; a transliteration into English or French is required. The name must be distinguishable from any existing registered name and must not contravene the misleading-name provisions of the Alberta Business Corporations Act.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 30 days of formal rejection, submit a written request for reconsideration to the Registrar of Alberta Corporate Registry, quoting the name search report number, the rejected name, a side-by-side comparison of proposed vs. confusingly similar names, and any ministerial consent/approval for restricted words. The Registrar decides under the Business Corporations Act; if the rejection is upheld, the applicant may file a new unconditional name reservation or seek judicial review in the Court of King's Bench of Alberta. No extension of an expired 90-day name reservation is available; a fresh search and reservation must be filed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permitted for the statutory registered office only if supplied by a licensed corporate/registered agent maintaining a physical street address in Alberta at which legal documents may be served. It is not accepted as the business-substance premise for an ISIC 4659 aviation parts distribution undertaking; the industry expectation is a maintained Alberta distribution facility or inventory/records location. A pure virtual-office setup for a trading ULC increases FINTRAC/bank suspicion and may be treated as absence of commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate: estimated 25-35% probability per annual compliance period of an unannounced inspection by CBSA, Transport Canada civil aviation inspectors, Alberta corporate registry examiners, or law-enforcement audits, principally because high-value surplus aircraft parts and controlled-goods/dual-use items attract enhanced scrutiny.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, ss 15–20 (unlimited liability corporation provisions); Alberta Corporate Registry procedures under the Corporate Registration System.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction (Corporate Registration System).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) filed under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an Alberta ULC; no escrow account required. Founders may subscribe for nominal share capital as set in the Articles.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, that the Corporation accepts the founders' subscription for an aggregate of 1,000 common shares at $0.01 per share, total stated capital $10,000, issued fully paid; and the directors are authorized to issue share certificates accordingly.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Corporation is established at [Address], [City], Alberta, with the Notice of Registered Office to be filed with the Alberta Corporate Registry.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name], [Name], and [Name] are appointed President, Secretary, and Chief Financial Officer, respectively, each to serve until the next annual meeting with authority to execute banking, lease, and regulatory documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry via NUANS Search System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS trademark and corporate name search through a registered service provider; reserve the chosen name for 90 days; ensure the corporate name includes the proper legal element 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' or 'ULC' as required under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as confusing or prohibited, either request a name review with the Corporate Registry or file a revised name reservation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Articles and Notices
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry – Corporate Registration System (CRS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft Articles of Incorporation in Form 1 designating the corporation as an unlimited liability corporation, setting out share structure, restrictions, directors, and registered office. Founders and initial directors must execute the documents; signatures should be notarized where required for foreign subscribers.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the articles, amend and refile; for substantive legal objections, request a Director’s ruling under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing and Payment of State Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry – CRS Electronic Filing Window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Articles and notices through the Corporate Registration System, pay the $350 state filing fee by credit card or authorized payment method, and retain the electronic filing receipt as proof of submission.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected, correct the flagged fields in CRS and resubmit; if the filing fee has been processed, obtain a refund or apply the credit to a new submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate and Opening of Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry – Registrar of Corporations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, obtain the Certificate of Incorporation; prepare the corporate minute book, adopt preliminary by-laws, issue share certificates to the founding shareholders, and maintain statutory registers of directors, officers, and shareholders.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If certificate issuance is delayed, contact the Registrar, request expedited service, or request an equivalent filing certificate for third-party verification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Filings and Municipal Business Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry and Municipal Licensing Authority (e.g., City of Calgary or Edmonton Licensing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the corporate initial return/notification with the Alberta Corporate Registry, adopt final corporate by-laws, appoint officers as resolved by the board, and apply for the municipal business licence authorizing warehouse and distribution of aviation parts.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For administrative non-compliance, pay late fees and file corrected returns; a municipal licence denial may be appealed to the local business licence appeal committee.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Transport Canada Civil Aviation Directorate – Commercial and Business Aviation
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Approved Maintenance Organization (AMO) Certificate – Parts Distribution (CAR 573) / Civil Aviation Parts Dealer Authorization

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – warehousing and distribution of non-hazardous surplus aircraft parts; registration required only if storage includes regulated hazardous materials or waste
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or VOC emission source expected; compliance with Alberta Waste Control Regulation (AR 192/1996), Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives, and Occupational Health and Safety Code limits if compressed gases, batteries, or fuel-contaminated components are stored.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the Alberta Fire Code (Safety Codes Act); structural load inspection of warehouse racking under the Alberta Building Code; and Alberta Occupational Health and Safety clearance for materials handling and storage of aviation components.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — federal and Alberta corporate income tax and GST/HST administration (T2 Corporate Internet Filing, GST/HST NETFILE, My Business Account); Alberta Treasury Board & Finance (ATBF) is nominal provincial authority but Alberta corporate tax is collected by CRA under the Tax Collection Agreement; registration of legal entity: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Ontario-equivalent is Alberta Corporate Registry/RegistryX). No separate provincial sales tax authority in Alberta.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Upon incorporation under the Alberta Business Corporations Act (RSA 2000, c B-9), the ULC files Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) to obtain its 9-digit CRA Business Number (BN) and associated program accounts: RC (GST/HST), RT (T2 corporate income tax), RP (payroll). The BN is the statutory tax identification number; no separate TIN/VAT ID exists. Non-resident parent/shareholders may be added by share transfer without re-registration; the ULC remains a Canadian resident corporation. For a foreign entity branch (non-ULC), the non-resident obtains a CRA BN for non-residents and registers extra-provincially under Alberta's Business Corporations Act/Part 21 of the Companies Act (OOP registration), but for this CA_AB ULC structure the standard domestic RC1 procedure applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Canada): ULC is deemed a corporation and a taxable Canadian corporation under ITA s. 83.4; files T2 and pays federal (15% general) and Alberta (8%) corporate income tax on worldwide income. Pass_Through_Eligible (US federal): disregarded-entity check-the-box election available on IRS Form 8832, creating hybrid-entity status; Canadian hybrid mismatch rules (ITA ss. 18.4, 18.6) apply. Territorial_Scope: not applicable — Canada taxes residents on worldwide income with foreign tax credits.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No Canadian check-the-box election. Key elections: (i) US IRS Form 8832 check-the-box to treat the Alberta ULC as disregarded/pass-through for US federal tax (hybrid entity) — must be filed within 75 days of formation or 12 months after any change; (ii) ITA s. 83.4(2) deeming provision confirming corporate status of ULC (no separate election needed); (iii) ETA Schedule IX Form GST20 election for closely related corporations (for GST pooling/organization); (iv) ITA s. 216(4) election for non-resident-owned rental property (not typically used by ULC trading company); (v) ITA s. 219 non-resident branch tax election (inapplicable to AB-resident ULC); (vi) Hybrid mismatch neutralization: careful application of ITA ss. 18.4/18.6 and US Reg. 1.1503/transition rules to avoid deduction/non-inclusion mismatches, plus s. 17.1 associated timing for unpaid amounts.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) / Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act (ETA); Alberta has no provincial sales tax (no PST), so only the 5% federal GST applies in Alberta; no separate provincial indirect tax on the distribution of aircraft parts.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — small supplier threshold: a person (including a non-resident) must be registered for GST/HST once worldwide taxable supplies (including zero-rated and excluding exempt supplies) exceed CAD 30,000 in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters or in a single calendar quarter for a start-up; once registered, the Alberta ULC charges 5% GST on domestic taxable supplies and 0% on exported goods/eligible offshore services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or CRA-API clearance exists in Canada. Voluntary PAN-Canadian e-Invoicing launched by the CRA using the PEPPOL framework (optional). Mandatory electronic filing: GST/HST registrants with taxable supplies exceeding CAD 1 million per year must file using GST/HST NETFILE or EDI; all T2 corporate returns must be filed electronically (EFILE/TEI) for corporations with gross revenue > CAD 1 million; electronic payment through the CRA's My Payment required for large remitters. The ULC must retain invoices (electronic or paper) meeting ETA s. 223(1) disclosure rules; foreign-language invoices require French/English translation on request.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supply of the surplus commercial aircraft rotables and avionics parts is zero-rated under ETA Schedule VI, Part V (Goods) if the ULC exports the goods as part of the supply: (a) ships/delivers them to a destination outside Canada (s. 5), (b) transfers possession to a common carrier/forwarding agent for export before consideration is due (s. 6), or (c) the goods are supplied for export with continued possession outside Canada (ss. 11-14). Related services provided to a non-resident (who is not registered and not carrying on business in Canada) are zero-rated under ETA Schedule VI, Part V (Services), s. 7; services in respect of the exported goods (repair, warehousing, freight logistics) are zero-rated under Part V, s. 12 (services to goods for export) etc. The ULC must satisfy the two-year evidence retention rule: proof of export (e.g., commercial invoice, air waybill, freight manifest) must be obtained no later than 2 years after the supply; otherwise the supply is re-characterized as taxable at 5%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Canada Customs B13A form or ACI eManifest for US-bound goods) — proof that the goods were exported from Canada and reported under the Customs Act for non-US destinations
Bill of Lading / original Air Waybill (Master and House) issued by a licensed carrier evidencing the aircraft parts left Canada and were consigned to the foreign air carrier/MRO
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 transfer receipt confirming foreign currency payment and FX repatriation into the ULC's Canadian bank account within the 180-day deadline

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current account convertibility under IMF Article VIII and the Bank of Canada Act. Capital account transactions require prior review by the Department of Finance for certain portfolio investments. Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are unrestricted subject to FINTRAC reporting thresholds of CAD 10,000. Key hurdles include mandatory PCMLTFA compliance, enhanced due diligence for aviation-sector clients, and prohibition on unlicensed cross-border money transmission.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or conversion ratio applies to export proceeds in Canada. Exporters must file Automated Export Reporting System (AERS) declarations with the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) for applicable shipments. Repatriation of foreign exchange receipts is required but occurs freely through licensed banks. All FX transactions exceeding reporting thresholds must be reported to FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility rating. Offshore digital EMIs are prohibited for aviation-parts distribution due to FINTRAC licensing requirements and Bank of Canada foreign exchange oversight. Legal constraints mandate use of traditional correspondent banking channels and prohibit unlicensed cross-border money transmission services.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote video KYC is permitted for Alberta ULC entities; however, directors and authorized signers must complete in-person or live video interviews during initial onboarding at tier-1 banks. Physical presence is mandatory for the first account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Undisclosed beneficial ownership or shell-company structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta Corporate Registry extract, director and UBO declarations, proof of source of funds, board resolutions, and incorporation documents

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transactions involving dual-use goods or high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: End-user certificates, Export Control List compliance documentation, valuation reports, and import/export licenses

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital must be routed via SWIFT MT103 wires using purpose codes such as 'EQUITY CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' or 'SHAREHOLDER LOAN'. Verification requires board resolutions, incorporation certificates, and source-of-funds evidence. All wires must reference the recipient account and be accompanied by remittance advice.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements cleared primarily through SWIFT MT103. Commercial Letters of Credit are available via correspondent banks. Escrow arrangements with licensed custodians are recommended for aviation-parts shipments to ensure compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (Registrar of Corporations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the anniversary date of incorporation each year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing after the one-month statutory period attracts a C$100 late-filing charge; continued default for two consecutive years enables administrative strike-off or dissolution by the Registrar after notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the corporation's tax year-end; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, the return is due by June 30.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure-to-file penalty under the Income Tax Act of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months, prescribed interest, CRA collection measures, and possible prosecution for repeat non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the fiscal year-end for an annual remitter; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, due by March 31.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure-to-file penalty of 5% of unremitted GST/HST plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months, prescribed interest on unpaid balances, offset of CRA refunds, and possible security requirements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T4 Statement of Remuneration and T4 Summary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the last day of February following the calendar year in which remuneration was paid.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties for late or incomplete information returns under the Income Tax Act, plus interest and CRA enforcement for continued non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue or asset threshold under the Alberta Business Corporations Act. A non-reporting private ULC may dispense with an independent auditor only by unanimous written shareholder consent for the fiscal year; an audit is mandatory if the corporation is a reporting issuer or if a shareholder or director removes the waiver.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is required for publicly accountable and reporting enterprises; a private Alberta ULC may elect Canadian ASPE or IFRS and must apply the chosen framework consistently.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta does not impose a standalone annual UBO declaration for an Alberta ULC. The annual return confirms the registered office and current directors only; share transfers are recorded in the Register of Transfers and the Register of Members at the time of transfer. Director changes must be reported to Alberta Corporate Registry within 15 days; beneficial-ownership information is maintained through the internal statutory register audit rather than a separate registry filing.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$5,000–US$15,000 if an independent audit becomes mandatory; nil where the unanimous waiver remains in force.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% (federal general corporate rate 15% + Alberta general corporate income tax rate 8%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No industry-specific statutory tax holiday. If the ULC qualifies as a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC), active business income up to CAD 500,000 is taxed at the federal small business rate of 9% (instead of the general 15%) and the Alberta small business rate of 4% (instead of the general 8%); otherwise the standard 23% effective rate applies. Other generic incentives such as the Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) tax credit and temporary full expensing allowances may apply only where eligible assets are used, but they are not industry-standard for surplus aviation parts distribution.
